title: New Jerusalem
summary: The eschatological city of Revelation 21-22 where God dwells with his people and creation is renewed.
historical_context: New Jerusalem appears as the final hope of the biblical story, reshaping Zion imagery after judgment and exile.
ancient_near_east_context: The vision reuses city and temple imagery familiar in the ancient world while transforming them around God’s direct presence.
literary_context: Revelation presents New Jerusalem as the climactic counterpart to Eden, Zion, and the temple.
covenantal_significance: The city pictures the consummation of covenant promise: God with his people in an unbroken, holy dwelling place.
interpretive_notes: Treat the vision as theological consummation, not merely a fantasy map of the afterlife.
The city image gathers Eden, temple, and Zion imagery into one final picture of presence and renewal.
common_questions: How does New Jerusalem relate to Eden and Zion?
Why does Revelation end with a city?

scripture_references.notes: the city named the LORD is there

related_objects.notes: no temple because God is present
